objectives.T53.04.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for local apic timers and interprocessor interrupts.
objectives.T53.04.b: Implement per-CPU timer interrupts and an IPI request/acknowledgment mailbox. Separate vector dispatch, end-of-interrupt and higher-level completion state.
objectives.T53.04.c: Show each CPU receiving its own timer events and complete a directed IPI round trip with a bounded timeout and matching sequence.
objectives.T53.05.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for smp spinlocks and interrupt context.
objectives.T53.05.b: Implement test-and-set and ticket locks, then compare with an MCS queue-lock model. Add IRQ-save wrappers that restore the previous local mask and audit lock ordering.
objectives.T53.05.c: Run multiple CPUs updating a protected invariant and reject the local-mask-only faulty variant. Measure contention and wait distributions separately from correctness.
objectives.T53.06.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for per-cpu ready queues.
objectives.T53.06.b: Implement per-CPU ready queues and fixed-affinity dispatch. Record transitions with CPU, task generation, old state and new state; validate the combined trace independently.
objectives.T53.06.c: Show actual task execution on all admitted CPUs with one-owner invariants and service accounting, then inject a duplicate enqueue that the checker rejects.
objectives.T53.07.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for remote wakeup and reschedule delivery.
objectives.T53.07.b: Implement remote wakeup with a generation-checked task handle and destination notification. Inject wakeups before idle check, between check and sleep, and during existing execution.
objectives.T53.07.c: Every accepted wake either makes the task runnable once or observes it already runnable. Retain a target trace showing remote progress after the receiving CPU was idle.
objectives.T53.08.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for affinity, migration and load balance.
objectives.T53.08.b: Add explicit affinity masks and migration of ready tasks, followed by a bounded work-balancing policy. Measure migration count, queue imbalance and cache-warmup cost.
objectives.T53.08.c: Show every migration has one source release and one destination acquisition, with no lost service or simultaneous execution. Explain why balancing overhead can reduce throughput.
objectives.T53.09.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for tlb shootdown and page reclamation.
objectives.T53.09.b: Implement bounded shootdown requests, local invalidation and acknowledgments before reclaim. Begin with one page and two CPUs using the same address space.
objectives.T53.09.c: Demonstrate that an old mapping cannot access a recycled frame after the completion boundary. A deliberately early-reclaim variant must fail a targeted interleaving test.
objectives.T53.10.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for parallel reduction with deterministic partitioning.
objectives.T53.10.b: Split an input range across1,2,4 CPUs with disjoint ownership, compute checked local sums and combine in fixed order. Include nondivisible lengths and empty partitions.
objectives.T53.10.c: Match a wide independent sum oracle, show distinct CPU execution and report wall time, CPU time and overhead. Do not infer physical speedup from emulator virtual CPU counts.
objectives.T53.11.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for bounded parallel work pool.
objectives.T53.11.b: Build a bounded shared work queue with original worker tasks, per-job IDs and a completion ledger. Compare static partitioning and dynamic dispatch for uneven job costs.
objectives.T53.11.c: Account for every submitted, rejected, completed and canceled job and show real execution on multiple CPUs. Diagnose one nested-submission deadlock.
objectives.T53.12.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for dependency dag execution and scaling limits.
objectives.T53.12.b: Implement bounded DAG validation, dependency counters and ready dispatch. Use a fork/join graph with unequal branch costs and compare1,2,4 CPU traces.
objectives.T53.12.c: Check topological precedence and one execution per node, compute work/span bounds independently, and explain observed scaling limits and failed-node propagation.
objectives.T54.01.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for dual images and static peripheral ownership.
objectives.T54.01.b: Build two original vector/startup/linker paths and an ownership table. Reserve nonoverlapping flash/RAM images plus an explicitly shared SRAM region and audit both map files.
objectives.T54.01.c: Cross-build both images with no forbidden dependencies and validate every declared range and owner. Physical boot remains a separate gate with exact board revision recorded.
objectives.T54.02.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for dual boot and epoch handshake.
objectives.T54.02.b: Implement explicit M7/M4 boot sequencing and a bounded shared-memory handshake using original register code. Clear only owned state and publish readiness after initialization.
objectives.T54.02.c: Capture distinct core start markers and matching epoch agreement. Inject a stale epoch in the model and demonstrate rejection; retain physical boot traces separately.
objectives.T54.03.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for shared-sram spsc channel.
objectives.T54.03.b: Implement two unidirectional SPSC channels with sequence and epoch fields. Use a fixed power-of-two capacity and explicit full/empty policy, then inspect emitted barriers.
objectives.T54.03.c: Transfer numbered payloads with no gaps except declared rejection, preserve slot ownership and compare payload checksums across cores. Require a real dual-core run for the physical gate.
objectives.T54.04.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for hsem and coalesced doorbells.
objectives.T54.04.b: Implement original HSEM take/release and notification handling with bounded ISR work. After waking, drain the SPSC channel and recheck the sleep boundary.
objectives.T54.04.c: Demonstrate a burst of several messages serviced after one coalesced wake and preserve every accepted sequence ID. Record ISR and task responsibilities separately.
objectives.T54.05.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for cache visibility and cache-line ownership.
objectives.T54.05.b: Create a cached transfer variant with aligned dedicated cache lines, clean before remote reads and invalidate before consuming remote writes as required. Include barriers and retain a cache-operation ledger.
objectives.T54.05.c: Compute rounded cache-line ranges independently, reproduce stale-data behavior under controlled conditions when observable, and demonstrate corrected payload checksums on hardware.
objectives.T54.06.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for dma buffers and cpu ownership transitions.
objectives.T54.06.b: Implement one bounded DMA transfer path using statically assigned channels and buffers. Publish completion with request generation and perform the chosen cache protocol before CPU consumption.
objectives.T54.06.c: Reconcile every buffer transition and verify payload bytes after actual DMA completion. Inject cancellation and stale-completion cases in the host model without claiming it simulates the bus.
objectives.T54.07.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for cross-core clocks and latency measurement.
objectives.T54.07.b: Measure request/response latency using same-core round trips and a shared logic-analyzer timebase. Record M7/M4 frequencies, timer widths, calibration and instrumentation overhead.
objectives.T54.07.c: Report distributions and upper observed values with sample count, clock conversion and uncertainty. Distinguish physical measurement from model timing and from an analytical WCET bound.
objectives.T54.08.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for peer failure and protocol recovery.
objectives.T54.08.b: Implement heartbeat/timeout observation and supervisor-driven epoch recovery. Stop a peer after publication and before acknowledgment, then reconcile retained or discarded work.
objectives.T54.08.c: Show stale epochs rejected, buffers returned through a defined recovery path and explicit uncertain-result reporting for a request interrupted across reset.
objectives.T54.09.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for interrupt-to-task pipelines on both cores.
objectives.T54.09.b: Build acquisition ISR to M4 task to shared queue to M7 worker to response pipeline. Give every hop a bounded queue and overload policy, then trace sequence IDs end to end.
objectives.T54.09.c: Reconcile accepted, completed and dropped items at every hop and derive an end-to-end latency budget from component observations with stated interference.
objectives.T54.10.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for amp end-to-end observatory.
objectives.T54.10.b: Package both ELF images, maps, protocol version and board configuration. Run periodic acquisition plus parallel compute, a queue-overload burst and a peer restart with external timing capture.
objectives.T54.10.c: Provide actual dual-core progress, queue and recovery traces with source/image hashes and a full RAM/CPU/I/O ledger. If hardware is unavailable, leave physical completion explicitly not-run.
objectives.T55.01.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for spsc publication and acquire-release ordering.
objectives.T55.01.b: Implement a fixed-capacity C atomic SPSC queue and a deliberately relaxed-publication model. State the happens-before chain and inspect the selected target instruction sequence.
objectives.T55.01.c: Validate sequence preservation and slot ownership under wrap and contention. Explain why failure to observe a relaxed-ordering defect on x86 does not prove portability.
objectives.T55.02.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for compare-and-swap and progress classifications.
objectives.T55.02.b: Implement an x86 CAS counter and a bounded model of interfering updates. Audit compiler atomic width and emitted instructions; keep allocation, logging and error paths in the progress analysis.
objectives.T55.02.c: Classify each operation progress property with explicit assumptions and show a schedule that starves one caller while others progress. Do not label that schedule wait-free.
objectives.T55.03.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for aba and identity reuse.
objectives.T55.03.b: Build a deterministic three-step stack model that pauses a reader, removes/reuses nodes and resumes its stale CAS. Compare raw pointers, tagged generations and deferred reuse.
objectives.T55.03.c: Show the exact corrupted history for raw-pointer CAS and state which assumption each mitigation adds. Distinguish ABA prevention from general use-after-free prevention.
objectives.T55.04.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for a bounded pool for concurrent nodes.
objectives.T55.04.b: Implement a fixed node arena with explicit free, live and retired states and generation IDs. Integrate a try-allocation result before linking a node into a queue.
objectives.T55.04.c: Reconcile all node states under exhaustion and contention, and include the free-list algorithm in the progress argument rather than treating it as magic infrastructure.
objectives.T55.05.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for hazard-pointer publication and reclamation.
objectives.T55.05.b: Implement a bounded hazard domain with fixed participants and retired lists. Enumerate protect-publish-recheck against remove-retire-scan, using conservative ordering before optimization.
objectives.T55.05.c: Demonstrate safe reuse only after the final hazard clears and report bounded-pool exhaustion when a reader stalls. Separate memory safety from progress and memory-usage guarantees.
objectives.T55.06.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for michael-scott queue with bounded reclamation.
objectives.T55.06.b: Implement the queue on x86 with supported CAS widths, explicit memory orders and protected node reads. Integrate empty, full-pool and help-tail paths and record operation histories.
objectives.T55.06.c: Check finite histories against FIFO semantics and demonstrate delayed-tail helping plus safe reclamation. Audit the entire call path before making a lock-free claim.
objectives.T55.07.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for epoch reclamation and quiescent states.
objectives.T55.07.b: Implement a fixed-participant epoch domain for an append/read/remove structure and compare retire-list growth with hazard pointers under a paused reader.
objectives.T55.07.c: Identify the earliest safe reuse point for each retired node and show memory retention under a nonquiescent reader. State that bounded storage can force explicit exhaustion despite algorithmic progress.
objectives.T55.08.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for read-copy-update as an ownership protocol.
objectives.T55.08.b: Implement immutable configuration replacement with fixed version slots and a bounded quiescent-state protocol. Keep writer serialization explicit and prevent mutation of published versions.
objectives.T55.08.c: Show each reader sees a self-consistent version and old storage remains valid through its final reader. Explain the selected grace-period model and its limits.
objectives.T55.09.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for concurrent histories and linearizability checking.
objectives.T55.09.b: Write a bounded backtracking checker for queue histories with distinct operation IDs. Feed generated legal histories and hand-designed lost-item, duplicate-item and ordering violations.
objectives.T55.09.c: Reject the supplied impossible histories and show a witness sequential order for accepted ones. State the history length/state-space limit and retain the smallest counterexample.
objectives.T55.10.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for end-to-end progress and contention audit.
objectives.T55.10.b: Compare SPSC, a mutex queue and the reclaimed MPMC queue under uncontended, contended, oversubscribed and paused-participant workloads. Audit all success, failure and reclamation paths.
objectives.T55.10.c: Publish correctness evidence separately from performance data, record uncertainty and classify progress for each complete operation. Explain an observed case where locking performs better.
objectives.T56.01.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for process and thread objects as distinct lifetimes.
objectives.T56.01.b: Refactor the existing one-thread process representation into bounded process and thread pools. Preserve old isolation tests and add two threads sharing one process mapping.
objectives.T56.01.c: Demonstrate shared user state within one process and isolation across two processes, with complete pool/refcount accounting after all threads exit.
objectives.T56.02.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for spawn, exit, wait and process reaping.
objectives.T56.02.b: Implement bounded spawn/exit/wait using the existing static ELF profile and boot archive. Test parent wait before and after child exit and define orphan handling.
objectives.T56.02.c: Run real child programs with distinct exit values and reject foreign/stale waits. Reconcile all resources on load failure and orphan cleanup.
objectives.T56.03.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for demand-zero faults and frame ownership.
objectives.T56.03.b: Implement demand-zero for one bounded heap region using the existing frame allocator. Decode fault cause and retain per-process page ledgers.
objectives.T56.03.c: Observe real first-touch faults and zero-filled bytes, show invalid accesses terminate the offending process, and verify no frame leaks across exhaustion and exit.
objectives.T56.04.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for restricted copy-on-write cloning.
objectives.T56.04.b: Implement the restricted clone and write-fault path with checked frame refcounts and rollback. Test parent and child writing separate values to the same virtual address.
objectives.T56.04.c: Demonstrate shared physical frames before writes and distinct contents afterward, including a sole-owner optimization and allocation-failure rollback.
objectives.T56.05.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for bounded process channels.
objectives.T56.05.b: Expose bounded send/receive/close syscalls using generation-checked endpoints. Start with fixed maximum message size and explicit directional rights.
objectives.T56.05.c: Run isolated client/server processes, reject invalid spans without kernel corruption and preserve queued-message accounting through peer exit.
objectives.T56.06.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for shared-memory objects and explicit synchronization.
objectives.T56.06.b: Implement bounded shared-memory create/map/unmap handles and one synchronized producer-consumer protocol. Keep executable mappings out of this teaching profile.
objectives.T56.06.c: Show one physical object visible through two virtual mappings with controlled publication, correct rights and final-reference reclamation.
objectives.T56.07.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for asynchronous block requests and completion ownership.
objectives.T56.07.b: Extend the original virtio block path with a bounded outstanding-request pool, generation IDs and wait queues. Preserve descriptor/buffer ownership through success, error and timeout observation.
objectives.T56.07.c: Run user work while actual block I/O is outstanding and account for all requests/descriptors. Demonstrate that timeout reports uncertainty without unsafe reuse.
objectives.T56.08.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for read-only boot archive as a file service.
objectives.T56.08.b: Implement a minimal read-only namespace and file operations over validated archive entries. Reuse the existing archive parser and reject writes or unsupported path syntax.
objectives.T56.08.c: Read known file hashes through the actual user syscall path and preserve independent offsets. Reject malformed archives before exposing any entries.
objectives.T56.09.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for vm execution as a bounded service.
objectives.T56.09.b: Wrap the existing VM in an isolated process service over channels. Add request IDs, bounded program/result messages and a clear cancellation/result-too-large policy.
objectives.T56.09.c: Run valid and malformed programs from separate clients, preserve process isolation and return explicit resource errors while other clients progress.
objectives.T56.10.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for single-owner persistent store service.
objectives.T56.10.b: Build a channel-based store service with bounded get/put requests, request IDs and one owner of the block handle. Reuse the existing WAL/checkpoint implementation unchanged behind the adapter.
objectives.T56.10.c: Preserve the store regression suite, show concurrent clients serialized through one owner and correlate durable replies with committed log records.
objectives.T56.11.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for service restart and reboot recovery.
objectives.T56.11.b: Integrate VM and store clients with supervised restart and the existing disk-recovery path. Persist a known value, terminate/restart the service, then reboot the guest and verify recovery.
objectives.T56.11.c: Recover the committed value after actual reboot, distinguish uncommitted work, and account for every request as completed, rejected or uncertain. Retain disk/image identities and restart traces.
objectives.T56.12.a: Derive and defend the state, ownership and ordering contract for physical dual-core application and os comparison.
objectives.T56.12.b: Integrate the accepted dual-core runtime, queues, notifications, cache/DMA rules and peer recovery. Record an end-to-end message ledger, deadline-miss policy and external timing captures.
objectives.T56.12.c: Deliver two audited images and actual physical evidence for parallel progress, synchronization, overload and restart. Keep any missing board gate explicitly open while retaining completed build/model evidence.
